sources: McKay, John G. More West Highland Tales. Vol. 2. Scottish Anthropological and Folklore Society. Edinburgh: Oliver and Boyd, 1969, 489.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The bodach is a Scottish folkloric figure, also called a carle. In the Highlands it could be a harmless trickster. As the Bodach Glas, or Dark Gray Man, it was a male banshee. It appeared just before a death. Its name marks its old-man look. It made beckoning signs or peered into windows after nightfall. It was more frightening than dangerous. The Bodach a Chipein, or Old Man with the Peg, was friendly and approachable. This Highland fairy watched humans at daily tasks. It wept whenever funerals went by. The word also appears in Ireland for the same figure.

okr.objective: Describe the bodach, a Scottish folkloric old-man figure.
key_results: The bodach is a Scottish folkloric figure.
